chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Touring Australia and its rugby league clubs
summary: In Australia they played rugby league clubs between Sydney and Melbourne, sat in with local musicians, and saw koalas and kangaroos.

story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: The mid-'50s. Now, when you went to -- how much do you remember of your performance and tour of Australia?

If I can remember, when we arrived in Australia, we -- it was Sidney, I believe it was -- and we toured quite a bit. We played places which they call -- you know the game that they have in Australia was called rugby --

-- and we played those, what they call the rugby league clubs. They had the clubs, special clubs, which were their nightclubs over there and recreation places, what they call rugby league clubs, which we played. We played several of them in different places outside between Melbourne and Sidney and a few other names, I can't remember. But we just had a ball, you know.
How did the Australian audiences strike you? Are they any different from American or European audiences?
No, they aren't any different. In fact, they loved us so very much. They had our recordings and to top it off, we had a chance of sitting in with -- on little sessions with Australian musicians.
Oh, they had some Australian jazz musicians.
Did you see any kangaroos or aborigines?
Yes, I did. Koala bears and what have you. It was real interesting, the little time that I had to get around while I wasn't playing, you know. Kangaroos, what have you.
Did you see any of those guys that use boomerangs to -- aborigines?
I didn't see any of those.
